title: JavaScript Classes Applied Check
description: Test your ability to predict class behavior with constructors, this, inheritance, super, static methods, getters, setters, private fields, and composition.
author: DailyCoder

questions.explanation: The constructor assigns the argument to `this.name`, so the instance stores `"Alice"`.

options.text: It creates a valid User instance
It throws because classes must be called with `new`

questions.explanation: Class constructors cannot be called like regular functions. They must be called with `new`.
Each call increments the same instance's `count` property.
In a derived class constructor, `super()` must run before accessing `this`.
`super.describe()` calls the parent method, and the child method adds extra text.

options.text: Throws because `add` is static and is not an instance method

questions.explanation: Static methods are called on the class, such as `MathUtils.add(2, 3)`, not on instances.
Getters are accessed like properties and compute a value when read.

options.text: It creates a private field automatically

questions.explanation: Assigning to `this.price` inside the `price` setter calls the same setter again. Use a different internal property.

options.text: Throws a syntax error because private fields cannot be accessed outside the class

questions.explanation: Private fields are only accessible inside the class body.
Public fields are per-instance. Incrementing `a` does not change `b.count`.

options.text: The method may lose its `this` context
Methods cannot be assigned to variables

questions.explanation: Extracting a method and calling it as a plain function can lose the original instance as `this`.

questions.prompt: Which design is better for `Car has an Engine`?
questions.explanation: `Car has an Engine` is a composition relationship, so passing an engine into the car is a better model.

questions.prompt: Which statement about methods declared in a class body is correct?

options.text: They are generally shared by instances through the prototype
They are recreated inside every constructor call automatically

questions.explanation: Class body methods are shared through the prototype, which is memory-efficient.

questions.prompt: When is a plain object probably better than a class?

options.text: When storing simple configuration data with no shared behavior
When creating many objects with shared methods
When a constructor must validate input

questions.explanation: Simple data without shared behavior is often clearer as a plain object.
